verdict.rationale: Discord documents an official REST API that apps authenticate to with a bot token or an OAuth2 bearer token. It also documents sending messages into channels (webhooks) and a Gateway for receiving server events, so an agent integration is plausible on first-party primitives. However, the evidence never explicitly documents reading channel message history, and token scoping is only implied by a single OAuth2 scope description, not shown for message read/post permissions. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of reading channel messages via API, documented message-related OAuth2 scopes or bot permission scoping, independent or hands-on corroboration of an agent workflow.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, I can have an agent read and post channel messages through the official API using scoped tokens

citations.quote: Authenticating with the Discord API can be done in one of two ways: 1. Using a bot token... 2. Using an OAuth2 bearer token
The Discord API is a REST API that allows you to interact with Discord data from your own applications.
Send messages into Discord channels or receive event notifications from Discord delivered to your app over HTTP.
The Gateway API lets apps open secure WebSocket connections with Discord to receive events about actions that take place in a server/guild
allows /users/@me/connections to return linked third-party accounts
